mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.1% over the prior month signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines below 0.1% for at least 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signal robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth and elevating equity valuations for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST and RSAFS above 12-month averages fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases cost of capital, reducing equity valuation multiples and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) relative to the prior quarter signals expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows positive quarterly growth.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) rising >0.5% month-over-month while FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% indicates low-cost consumer spending environment, accelerating revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 0.5% fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: PAYEMS increasing for three consecutive months after a 2% decline signals labor market recovery, boosting consumer spending and corporate hiring for positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rising for 3 months after 2% decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS shows three consecutive months of growth after a 2% decline.
